newsitem.title: FRANCE: UNESCO panel okays pact on genetic research ethics.
newsitem.headline: UNESCO panel okays pact on genetic research ethics.

text.p: A UNESCO expert committee on Tuesday approved a draft declaration of ethical guidelines for genetic research which declares the genetic material in every human to be "the common heritage of humanity".

UNESCO -- the U.N. Educational Scientific and Cultural Organisation -- said the draft, in the works for the past three years, would next be submitted to a panel of government experts who plan to meet in July 1997.
After that it would be referred to UNESCO member states, with an eye to its adoption as an international convention before the end of next year.

The draft declaration states that human genetics research holds vast potential but must be regulated to protect public health and guard against any practice that "runs counter to human dignity and human rights".
It cautions that peoples' genetic makeup should never be used as a basis for granting or denying their rights.
Approval by the UNESCO experts came two months after the agency's International Bioethics Committee (IBC) objected to parts of the draft and sent it back to a subcommittee for fine tuning.
The subcommittee revised the draft during a two-day session which ended on Tuesday, UNESCO's statement said.

UNESCO created the IBC in 1993 to monitor developing ethical issues in genetic research and engineering. Its 55 experts come from 40 countries and include doctors, scientists, philosophers and lawyers.
